newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Budapest BUX loses half percent in profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Budapest BUX loses half percent in profit-taking.

text.p: Hungarian share prices closed mixed bringing down the BUX index from its peak on the Budapest Stock Exchange on Thursday in an apparent sign that many investors are beginning to lock in profits, traders said.
But market participants said it was a healthy correction rather than a case of investors fleeing the market, after an around 30 percent rise of the index since the beginning of the year.
"There was some profit-taking," said Balazs Szabo of Eastbrokers. "But otherwise money continues to flow into the market."
"The fact that the market is coming a little lower is to be regarded as a normal reaction to serious price rises," another trader said earlier today.
The trader said astute foreign investors may reduce their presence on the Hungarian market but there were no signs of them leaving it completely.
"Key foreign investors are reducing their exposure on the market but they aren't turning away from it," this trader said.
On Thursday losers were led by the banks and chemicals stocks.

Inter-Europa Bank, which surged in one single deal to 63,000 forints on Wednesday, ended at 56,000, down 7,000. OTP, also strong gainer yesterday, lost almost seven percent and finished at 3,870, down 280.
The chemicals continued the fall they began yesterday. Borsodchem eased two and half percent to finish at 5,900 forints, down 150, while TVK ended at 2,540, down 60.
Elsewhere on the market, the pharmaceuticals closed mixed. Egis jumped to a new record high of 11,800, before it retreated to close at 11,770, up 470.
Richter and Human headed lower to end the day at 11,300, down 100, and at 3,350, down 80, respectively.
Plastics maker Pannonplast lost 75 forints to finish at 7,050, while home improvement product maker Graboplast jumped to a new high of 8,600 forints. It closed at the new peak, up 300.
